---
title: "Examples"
subtitle: "Folded output you can open."
description: "Cell output folded by the extension as this page runs, one section per option, with the cell that produced each."
---

Every fold below was produced by the extension as this page was rendered, from a cell that actually ran.
The site sets these defaults in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
extensions:
  collapse-output:
    method: lua
    default-open: false
    summary-template: "{type} ({lines} lines)"
    summaries:
      stdout: "Console output"
      stderr: "Warnings and errors"
```

## Folding one cell

```{python}
#| echo: fenced
#| output-fold: true

for i in range(24):
    print(f"line {i}")
```

The summary comes from `summaries.stdout`, which this site sets to "Console output".

## A summary of your own

```{python}
#| echo: fenced
#| output-fold: true
#| output-summary: "Click to view the results"

for row in [(n, n * n, n ** 3) for n in range(1, 13)]:
    print(f"{row[0]:>3} {row[1]:>5} {row[2]:>7}")
```

`output-summary` beats both `summaries` and `summary-template`.

## Starting open

```{python}
#| echo: fenced
#| output-fold: true
#| output-open: true

print("This output starts visible.")
print("The reader can fold it away.")
```

`output-open` overrides the document's `default-open`, which is `false` here.

## Warnings and errors

Output on the error stream is folded separately, and takes its own summary.

```{python}
#| echo: fenced
#| output-fold: true

import sys

print("A result on the standard stream.")
print("A warning on the error stream.", file=sys.stderr)
```

`summaries.stderr` labels that one, and `output-types` restricts folding to the kinds of output you name.

## Rich output

A plot is display output rather than console text, so it is folded under its own type.

```{python}
#| echo: fenced
#| output-fold: true
#| output-summary: "The figure"

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

figure, axes = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3))
axes.plot([n * n for n in range(12)], marker="o")
axes.set_title("Squares")
plt.show()
```

## A template rather than fixed text

`summary-template` fills in `{type}` and `{lines}`, so a reader knows the size of what they are opening before they open it.

```yaml
extensions:
  collapse-output:
    summary-template: "{type} ({lines} lines)"
```

The cell below sets no summary of its own and no entry in `summaries` covers its type, so the template is used:

```{python}
#| echo: fenced
#| output-fold: true

from IPython.display import Markdown

Markdown("\n".join(f"- item {n}" for n in range(1, 9)))
```

## Folding everything

Rather than marking each cell, fold the lot and opt out where it matters:

```yaml
extensions:
  collapse-output:
    collapse-all-outputs: true
```

```{python}
#| echo: fenced
#| output-fold: false

print("This one stays visible, because the cell opts out.")
```

`output-fold: false` on a cell still wins, so a plot worth seeing stays visible.

Pair it with `auto-collapse-size` to fold only what is actually long:

```yaml
extensions:
  collapse-output:
    collapse-all-outputs: true
    auto-collapse-size: 20
```

Outputs of twenty lines or more are forced closed, whatever `default-open` says.
